DILG BAGONG P'L'P'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT OILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City NO. S. 2025 MR. RUPERTO BUSCATO lifeaidphil@yahoo.com Dear Mr. Buscato: This has reference to your request for legal opinion, as conveyed in your electronic mail dated 8 November 2024, in which you raised the following queries, to wit: 1. Can a barangay kagawad directly disburse funds from the barangay treasurer for utilization in the implementation of projects and programs? (sic) 2. Is it lawful for a barangay kagawad to be allocated budget for his committee programs and projects and disburse the same, to personally use the funds in doing such program? (sic) Following our request for clarification on the matter, you provided further context to these queries in your email dated 29 November 2024, received by this Office on 2 December 2024, explaining that each Sangguniang Barangay member (SB member) formulates a budget for their respective committees and directly withdraws funds from the Barangay Treasurer to implement their respective programs. Hence, we gathered, that you are asking for the propriety of this practice. For your first query, we posit in the affirmative. Funds may be disbursed to an elective official, e.g. a Sangguniang Barangay member, for the implementation of a project or program he/she is spearheading, provided that there is an appropriations ordinance authorizing the disbursement, and the said project or program is included in the reviewed annual budget of the barangay. To elaborate, we wish to discuss at this point, the matter of approving barangay annual budgets, which cover appropriations for development projects, as well as provisions for the delivery of basic services. The barangay annual budget is prepared by the Punong Barangay for the ensuing fiscal year, and is authorized through the enactment of an appropriations ordinance by majority of the SB members.l This approval of the ordinance by the SB concerned is solely a barangay matter, and the said ordinance is validly enforceable at the beginning of the ensuing calendar, despite pending review of the same by the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan, through the city or municipal budget officer, pursuant to the mandate of Section 333 of the LGC. I Section 331 of the Local Government Code. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

In DILG Opinion No. 62, series of 2023, this Department has discussed that: "Xxx The Code is clear in that the approval of ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay is contingent upon the approval of the majority of all its members — by 'its' meaning the sangguniang barangay members concerned — after which the punong barangay shall sign such ordinance. Accordingly, the approval of sangguniang barangay ordinances is solely a barangay matter — the Code does not require the involvement of the city/municipal mayor or the sangguniang panlungsod or bayan for that matter. After approval, the ordinance authorizing the barangay annual budget shall be transmitted to the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan, through the city or municipal budget officer, for review pursuant to the mandate of Section 333 of the LGC At this junction, may we stress that pending review by the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan, such barangay ordinance authorizing the annual budget can be validly enforced (e.g. funds can already be disbursed) because effectivity is determined not upon review thereof but rather in accordance with Section 332 of the LGC. Hence, the ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing calendar year. Said ordinance authorizing the annual budget shall continue to be in full force and effect unless and until within sixty (6) days from receipt of the said ordinance, the sangguniang panglungsod/bayan shall have ascertained that the ordinance contains appropriations in excess of the estimates of the income duly certified as collectible, or that the same has not complied with the budgetary requirements set forth in Title V, in which case, the said ordinance would be inoperative upon declaration by the sanggunian to that effect. With the advice of such action taken by the sanggunian, the latter shall retum the barangay ordinance, through the city or municipal budget officer, to the punong barangay for proper adjustments. " In fine, we restate that so long as the project/program being implemented is included in the approved annual budget, as well as in the development plan of the barangay, the funds for the same may be disbursed in accordance with the appropriations ordinance of that barangay. Nowhere can we find in the Local Government Code, pertinent laws, or in jurisprudence, a prohibition on the disbursement of funds to a Sangguniang Barangay member, as the release and disbursement of barangay funds is even governed by a principle stating that fiscal responsibility shall be shared among all barangay officials exercising authority over the financial affairs, transactions, and operations of the barangay. In relation to foregoing, and to answer your second query, several laws have mandated the creation of different barangay committees/councils, such as the following to wit: a) Executive Order No. 63, series of 1993 for the creation of a Barangay Physical Fitness and Sports Development Council; b) Executive Order No. 366, series of 1996 and DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2015-130 for the creation of a Barangay Peace and Order Committee; c) Republic Act NO. 9003 for the creation of a Barangay Ecological Solid Waste Management Committee; 2 of 3

d) The Child and Youth Welfare Code for the organization of the Local Council for the Protection of Children; and e) several laws, including Republic Act No. 9165, for the establishment of a Barangay Anti-Drug Abuse Council. With these mandates, it is only proper that funds be allocated to each committee to support the implementation of the programs and activities aligned to carry out their respective functions. But as to whom the funds shall be disbursed, we are constrained from competently answering the same, considering that it can only be determined through a review of the ordinance authorizing such disbursement. We opine, however, that if an ordinance authorizes the disbursement of funds to a committee chairperson, who is a Sangguniang Barangay member, for the execution of programs related to the committee they head, such disbursement is proper. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have enlightened you on this matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs 3 of 3
